clue.text: Guy auditioned in armour

indicators.note: something auditioned is heard, so the word for guy is taken by its sound

parts.note: a guy is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A man tried out for a part while wearing a suit of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditioned' says the word for Guy, MALE, is heard, not seen; it sounds like MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is flexible body protection made of interlinked metal rings, as in chain mail.

clue.text: Asleep uncomfortably in wood

indicators.note: sleeping uncomfortably suggests tossing about, so the letters of asleep are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has dozed off awkwardly in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapele is an African hardwood timber, similar to mahogany.

clue.text: Touch screens regularly finding applications

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every third letter of the phrase touch screens

explanation.surface: Tapping touch screens at intervals to locate the apps on a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks every third letter of TOUCH SCREENS: the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th.
explanation.definitionFit: Uses are purposes or employments, the ways something is applied.

clue.text: 10 low scores by clubs?

definitions.meaning: birds, so fliers, the answer to 10 Across
in golf an eagle is a score of two under par on a hole, made with clubs

explanation.surface: Clubs posting poor results, as in a sports league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like football clubs, fitting the theme (Crystal Palace are the Eagles), but here it is golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles are large birds of prey, and also golf scores two strokes under par.

clue.text: Poach trout to begin with, adding last of asparagus spears chopped up

indicators.note: to begin with means only the opening letter of trout is used
chopping something up breaks it into pieces that are rearranged, here the letters of spears with the extra letter
last of means the final letter of asparagus

explanation.surface: A recipe: poach the trout first, then add chopped asparagus spears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges SPEARS into RESPAS; the recipe surface hides that poach means trespass to hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To poach is to hunt or fish illegally on someone else's land, which is trespassing.

clue.text: Sealed item Charles almost smashed

indicators.note: something smashed is broken apart, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the name Charles loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Charles nearly broke a packaged item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CHARLES to CHARLE; 'smashed' rearranges ITEM with CHARLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermetical means airtight, closed so tightly that nothing can get in or out.

clue.text: How to conserve and raise exotic 10?

parts.note: canning is a way of preserving food

indicators.note: exotic means foreign or unusual, so the letters of raise take an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about keeping and breeding foreign birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' shuffles RAISE into ARIES. The answer is also the nickname of Norwich City football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaries are small songbirds, so they are fliers (10 Across).

clue.text: Mo preserves bronze with fallen head

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, falls down to the bottom of the down entry, moving from the front to the end

parts.note: preserves can be tins, containers of preserved food
bronze as a skin colour is a tan

explanation.surface: A man named Mo keeps bronze and has had a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with fallen head' moves the first T of TINSTAN to the end. Mo is short for moment, a common crossword usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mo, short for moment, is a very short time, as in 'wait a mo', so an instant.

clue.text: 10's warm and dry hands

parts.note: to air clothes is to warm and dry them, as in an airing cupboard
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: A description of the warm, dry hands of the fliers.
explanation.walkthrough: To air laundry is to warm and dry it, so the whole phrase is one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are aviators, people who fly, so fliers (10 Across).

clue.text: Absconders are still in France, approaching south

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so south comes next
in places the word for are still inside the abbreviation for France

parts.note: to lie is to be still, as in lie low

explanation.surface: Runaways who remain in France as they head south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absconders' looks like the subject of the sentence, and it is: fliers here are those who flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Fliers here are those who flee, people who run away, as absconders do.

clue.text: Brownie in crowd returning to base as before

indicators.note: in puts the word for Brownie inside the reversed crowd
returning means the word for crowd is read backwards

parts.note: a crowd is a mass of people
a brownie is a household spirit, an elf
E is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A Brownie in a crowd heading back to base as she did before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the crowd word to SSAM. Brownie suggests the junior Girl Guide, but it is the household sprite. E as base comes from mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfsame means the very same, identical with what was mentioned earlier.

clue.text: Second assailant sets about shop worker

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A second attacker sets upon a shop employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges S, ASSAILANT and SETS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales assistant serves customers in a retail shop.

clue.text: Rock bottom? Well, I'm a lot different

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters of the phrase are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone at their lowest says they feel much better now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges WELLIMALOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time low is the lowest level ever reached, the very bottom.

clue.text: 10 faint on board

indicators.note: on, read with board, means aboard, so the faint word sits inside the ship

parts.note: board here stands for a ship, the steamship abbreviated SS
faint or pale means wan

explanation.surface: Someone passes out on a ship or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention: inside SS, short for steamship. Swansea City's nickname is the Swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Swans are large waterbirds that fly, so they are fliers (10 Across).

clue.text: Trailing about somewhat to find bones

indicators.note: about means the run taken is turned round and read backwards
somewhat means only part of the word trailing is taken

explanation.surface: A detective trailing someone around hoping to find remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes AILI from inside TRAILING; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The ilia are the hip bones, plural of ilium.

clue.text: Margaret breaking scholar Giovanni's heart? It strikes a chord

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the pet name goes inside
the heart of the phrase scholar Giovanni is its central run of letters

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret interrupts a scholar named Giovanni, perhaps touching his feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the central five letters of SCHOLARGIOVANNI read as one run, ARGIO; 'breaking' splits it open for the pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio plays the notes of a chord one after another, a broken chord struck in sequence.

clue.text: See 28
Sign from second corporation to land on moon?

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece landing on the other sits beneath it, so it comes after

parts.note: CORP is the abbreviation for corporation
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A second company plans a moon landing.
explanation.walkthrough: IO, a moon of Jupiter, comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is a sign of the zodiac, the scorpion.

clue.text: Party time on tick?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the letter for time follows

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second, abbreviated SEC

explanation.surface: A political party running on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit, but tick here is a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a faction or group with shared beliefs, as a party is.

clue.text: Naive girl, enmeshed by the setter's importuning, bolted from time to time

indicators.note: enmeshed by means the girl's name is caught inside the other pieces

parts.note: the setter's means I am, contracted to IM
importuning is pressing, press

indicators.note: from time to time means only every other letter of bolted is used

parts.note: Iona is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A naive girl caught up in the setter's pleading, then running off now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes the odd letters of bolted; 'enmeshed by' sets the girl between IMPRESS and those letters. Press here is a noun, an urging.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressionable people are easily influenced, as the naive and inexperienced are.

clue.text: Secure both ends of excavation on slope

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word for slope follows
both ends of means just the first and last letters of excavation

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Shoring up a dig site on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is the ends of excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist help or support is to secure or obtain it.

clue.text: Impromptus, primarily from Alexander Scriabin, including early pieces from Debussy, Liszt, Ibert and Bartok

indicators.note: including means the first pair holds the other four letters within it
primarily means the first letters of the two names of the Russian composer
early pieces from means the opening letter of each of the four composers

explanation.surface: A recital of short improvised piano works by Scriabin, Debussy, Liszt, Ibert and Bartok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts DLIB inside AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is something unplanned or improvised; ad libs are lines delivered off the cuff.

clue.text: Loop back within Cork with son to see 10

indicators.note: within puts the reversed loop inside the word for cork

parts.note: to cork a bottle is to seal it

indicators.note: back means the word for loop is read in reverse

parts.note: a lug is a loop or handle

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit Cork with your son to watch the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city but is a verb, to seal. 'back' reverses the loop word and 'within' puts it inside. Brighton's football club is nicknamed the Seagulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Seagulls are coastal birds, so fliers (10 Across).

clue.text: P's out of training?

definitions.meaning: in music p, for piano, marks a passage to be played ...
someone out of training is unfit

explanation.surface: Asking whether P is out of practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft means quiet in music, and flabby or unfit in body.

clue.text: Head's rested on this rugby ball perhaps — that hurt!

parts.note: pill is slang for a ball used in sport, a rugby ball for one
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A rugby player with a sore head cries out after a ball strikes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is the cushion a sleeper rests their head on in bed.

clue.text: 10 headless chickens

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: chickens are fowls

explanation.surface: Fliers rushing about like headless chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday's nickname is the Owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are nocturnal birds of prey, so fliers (10 Across).

clue.text: 10 dismissed at the Oval, say, by Lock's return

indicators.note: by means next to, so the reversed lock follows

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out, a way of being dismissed

indicators.note: return means the word for lock is turned back

parts.note: a snib is a catch or bolt, a lock

explanation.surface: Fliers out at a cricket match after a bowler named Lock throws the ball back.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, so dismissal there suggests cricket; run out is RO. 'return' turns SNIB into BINS. Lock was also an England bowler. Bristol City are the Robins.
explanation.definitionFit: Robins are small red-breasted songbirds, so fliers (10 Across).

clue.text: Bolts meat loaf — originally for 7, 23, 27, 4, 14, 26

indicators.note: originally signals a rearrangement, as if the words were back in a different, original order

explanation.surface: Someone gobbles meat loaf, which was first made for these clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLTSMEATLOAF has exactly the letters needed. The six answers referenced are all football club nicknames: Norwich, Brighton, Bristol City, Crystal Palace, Swansea and Sheffield Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the referenced answers is the nickname of an English or Welsh professional soccer club.
